subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance permanently use this separate opt-in millisecond timeout and host-owned fence, or should it share an existing compaction/runtime timeout contract?
rationale: Both approaches can bound the stall, but they create different public configuration semantics and upgrade behavior; repository policy requires owner intent rather than inferring a new long-term config contract from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Approve dedicated opt-in timeout
options.body: Keep the new key disabled by default and accept the host-owned lane-release and fencing contract demonstrated by this PR.

options.title: Reuse an existing timeout
options.body: Refactor maintenance to an established compaction or runtime timeout contract, with explicit compatibility behavior and proof for existing plugins.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep the issue and PR open until the plugin cancellation and maintenance lifecycle contract is defined more broadly.

recommendation.title: Approve dedicated opt-in timeout
recommendation.body: Keep the new key disabled by default and accept the host-owned lane-release and fencing contract demonstrated by this PR.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the strongest available owner-routing signal in the PR timeline for the context-engine/session decision.
